title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
source: canonical Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is the root node of a binary tree whose values may be negative. A path is any chain of nodes connected by parent-child links, and it must contain at least one node; it may start and end anywhere. Return the largest sum of node values along any path.
constraints: the tree stays balanced enough that recursion is safe

examples.explanation: The path must contain one node, so a lone negative is the answer.

hints: A path through a node combines the best downward runs from its two children, plus the node itself.
A downward run that would sum negative is better replaced by nothing at all: clamp each side at zero.
While computing the best downward gain per node, fold node + left gain + right gain into a running best; all-negative trees end with the largest single value.
solution: Single post-order walk: each node returns its best downward gain (clamped at zero) and folds node + left + right into a running best. O(n) time, O(depth) stack space.
failureHint: hidden tests include all-negative trees and a single node

visible.failNote: the path may cross the root from one subtree to the other
the path must contain at least one node
